note.text: Mediterranean-type climates have generally hot or warm dry summers and milder wetter winters. They occur around the Mediterranean Sea and in other western-margin regions, including parts of California, central Chile, the Cape and southwestern Australia. Seasons reverse between hemispheres. Vegetation often includes evergreen shrubs and trees with small tough leaves; woodland and more open formations vary with site and disturbance. Summer drought influences growth, fire risk and cultivation. The biome is not defined by rain falling only in the warmest season.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to relate dry summers and wetter winters to plant adaptations and seasonal land-use constraints. Builds on: hot-desert aridity and seasonal vegetation responses. Leads to: comparing Cameroon’s environments with global biome patterns.

sections.heading: Explain the geography
sections.text: Mediterranean-type climates have generally hot or warm dry summers and milder wetter winters. They occur around the Mediterranean Sea and in other western-margin regions, including parts of California, central Chile, the Cape and southwestern Australia. Seasons reverse between hemispheres. Vegetation often includes evergreen shrubs and trees with small tough leaves; woodland and more open formations vary with site and disturbance. Summer drought influences growth, fire risk and cultivation. The biome is not defined by rain falling only in the warmest season.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: The chart is an invented northern-hemisphere record with summer dryness and wetter cooler-season months. A southern-hemisphere example would shift the seasonal calendar. Olives, vines and other crops are associated with parts of Mediterranean agriculture, but their viability depends on local conditions and management. Irrigation may supplement water but has costs and resource limits. Cameroon’s tropical seasons should not be relabelled Mediterranean merely because some months are dry.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: State which hemisphere is used before naming summer months. Explain how tough leaves or seasonal growth help with drought, without treating all shrubs as identical. A humid winter and dry summer are a pattern, not a promise that every year has equal rain. Compare climate evidence rather than assigning a biome from a crop name alone.

small tough leaves helping plants cope with seasonal stress
opposite seasonal calendars north and south of the Equator
a limit affecting how people use seasonal water and land

mistake.right: a dry period coinciding with the warm season.
mistake.why: The characteristic contrast is dry summer and wetter cooler season.

cards.idea: Distinguish the features before applying them.
example: summer drought: a dry period coinciding with the warm season.
sclerophyll feature: small tough leaves helping plants cope with seasonal stress.
hemisphere contrast: opposite seasonal calendars north and south of the Equator.
resource constraint: a limit affecting how people use seasonal water and land.

questions.prompt: Read the invented monthly rainfall chart. Add the labels above all monthly bars to obtain the annual total in mm; the vertical-axis tick labels are not extra observations.

misconceptions.explain: That is a monthly mean, not the sum for the year.
That is the difference between wettest and driest months, not the annual total.
That multiplies an already millimetre total by ten without a unit conversion.

solution: The annual rainfall of this classroom record is {answer} mm. A real biome classification also needs temperature and other evidence.

right.text: summer drought: a dry period coinciding with the warm season.

right.text: sclerophyll feature: small tough leaves helping plants cope with seasonal stress.

right.text: hemisphere contrast: opposite seasonal calendars north and south of the Equator.
